set_text.text: A par level is the full mark for one line: the stock level each order brings it back up to. The order is the gap between today's count and that mark. At 120 cases a day, a 7 day cycle and 2 buffer days, the mark is 1,080 cases.
The whole gap between two deliveries, plus your reserve. That is why par should look high on delivery day: it has to last until the next truck.
Which days run busy. Par prices every day at the average, so a short cycle that holds your heaviest days draws on the 2 buffer days.
The $23,760 at par is the most the line holds, on delivery day. Across the cycle the floor averages well below it, and that average is what carrying costs run on.
Who uses a par level calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who restock their own warehouse on a regular delivery cycle. Anyone who sizes the next top up order, or answers for the cash it ties up, should run it.
